The student is able to demonstrate generic programming abilities in Python, i.e. being able to set up an algorithm based on input/output, variables and functions, computations and control statements.

objectives and content
    Objectives

The student understands the following topics: existence and origin of numerical errors, solution techniques for (systems of) linear and non-linear equation(s). 
The student understands the fundamental principles for solving linear and non-linear algebraic and differential equation solvers, and being able to implement basic solution methods. 
The students is able to use Python functionalities and NumPy/SciPy/Matplotlib features to solve a wide range of Chemical Engineering problems (solving ODEs, optimisation problems, interpolation and integration). 
The student is able to validate, verify and classify solution techniques according to the order of convergence, absolute and relative error. 
The student is able to formulate solution strategies for chemical engineering questions, by identification of the equation type and consequently breaking down the problem into sizable parts and suggesting the right numerical tool(s) (e.g. solution techniques for systems of linear and non-linear algebraic and (partial) differential equations, optimization problems, numerical integration and interpolation), and being able to implement them into a script or program. 
The student is able to demonstrate generic programming abilities in Python, i.e. being able to set up an algorithm based on input/output, variables and functions, computations and control statements. 

    ContentThis course teaches the following concepts in the field of Numerical Methods: Programming and Algorithms, Numerical Errors (and stability) in computer simulations, Linear Equations: matrix calculations (inverse, determinant ), Gaussian elimination, Partial Pivot Ting, LU factorization, sparse systems, iterative methods (Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel), Non-Linear equations: Newton's method Broyden’s method, Numerical interpolation and integration, Ordinary differential equations (explicit/implicit methods, systems of ODEs, higher-order methods), Partial differential equations (discretization, implicit and explicit solutions, time stepping, characterization of PDE), and Optimization and data regression (Simplex method, least squares method) 

Extra information about the assessment
'TA’s will not be involved in the evaluation of friends or relatives and will not give any preferential treatment to others.'

4 assignments, each 20% of the final result, that consist of an assignment done in groups of 2 people and the results will be addressed in a short report. The lecturers and/or PhD students will be grading the summative assignments 2, 3 and 4. I will use peer-assessment for the grading of the first summative assignments. The quality of the individually performed peer-review will also be part of the grade in the form of a factor that can vary between 0,8 and 1,2. This factor, multiplied with the mean grade from the peer-review gives the final grade for each assignment. There is a possibility to challenge flawed peer-review in order to remove them from the grade averaging. The exact arrangements for performing the peer review are given in the study guide and during the first lecture.
The final exam consists of an individual, supervised exam that combines programming skills and insight in the subject matter, which will cover all topics discussed in class. The final exam counts for 20% in the final grade. The final course grade will be the weighted average, which should be at least a 5.5 to pass the course. A student that has participated in the final exam, but has gotten a lower mark than a 5.5 for the final exam is awarded a NVD as final result, even when the weighted average of the results of all assignments and final exam yields a 5.5 or higher. The course is successfully completed when the final result is a 6 or higher.

All results of the assignments and final assignment are only valid in the academic year in which the assignments have been performed. For students who followed Numerical Methods (6BER03) and did not successfully finalize the individual assignment (notebook exam), and who have requested an extended validity for the assignments with the responsible lecturer, the following applies:
The results of the (interim) assignments are treated as a joined set and are valid for a period of 2 years. The results of the assignments that will be used in combination with the final exam, are the final assignment results of assignment 1 (including peer review component), and the final assessment of assignments 2, 3 and 4. It is not possible to select/combine assignment results from different academic years.

    Short promotional description of the courseThis course introduces the basics of numerical methods and scientific computing. After this course students understand the concepts, and are able to recognize and solve (systems of) linear, nonlinear, and differential equations, as well as numerical interpolation and integration. The mathematical and numerical background of several numerical techniques will be introduced and the key concepts will be implemented and demonstrated. Python is used as the main programming environment, introducing also the functionalities provided by the modules NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib.
